yoyaku.midashi: Green Day — “Wake Me Up When September Ends”
yoyaku.text:
September has an ending.
Some memories don’t.

Green Day — “Wake Me Up When September Ends”

A quiet ache hiding inside a rock anthem.

#GreenDay
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=green-day&song=wake-me-up-when-september-ends

A song that feels like autumn in Japan.

Momoe Yamaguchi — 秋桜 (Cosmos)

A daughter, her mother, and the quiet days before leaving home.
Simple, tender, unforgettable.

#MomoeYamaguchi #山口百恵
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=momoe&song=cosmos

Some records fill a room.
This one empties it.

Nick Drake — “Pink Moon”

One voice, one guitar, nothing in the way.
Best played early, before the day starts talking.

#NickDrake
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=nicholas-drake&song=pink-moon

Two cities, one moon, and a phone call that fixes nothing.

Ayaka — 三日月 (Mikazuki), “Crescent Moon”

A Japanese ballad about loving someone who is too far away. She holds it back until the last chorus, then lets go.

#Ayaka #絢香
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=ayaka&song=mikazuki

A folk tune far older than the two men who made it famous.

Simon & Garfunkel — “Scarborough Fair”

Two voices, close enough to sound like one.
It turns a grey morning into something you wanted anyway.

#SimonAndGarfunkel
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=simon-garfunkel&song=scarborough-fair

If midnight had a color, it might sound like this.

EGO-WRAPPIN’ — 色彩のブルース
(Shikisai no Blues)

Jazz, blues, and one of Japan’s great late-night voices.

#EGOWRAPPIN #エゴラッピン
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=ego-wrappin&song=shikisai-no-blues

An invitation, sung at the volume of someone still half asleep.

Norah Jones — “Come Away with Me”

Piano, brushes, and a voice that never raises itself.
Good for the first hour of a day you don’t want to rush.

#NorahJones
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=norah&song=come-away-with-me

A love song for two people who feel like visitors on their own street.

KIRINJI — エイリアンズ (Aliens)

A sleeping city, and the strange comfort of being the only ones awake.

#KIRINJI #キリンジ
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=kirinji&song=aliens

Some songs are built for the last hour of the night.

Neil Young — “Harvest Moon”

Brushed drums, a slow sway, and a man asking someone he has known for decades to dance with him again.

#NeilYoung
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=neil-young&song=harvest-moon

yoyaku.midashi: Tatsuro Yamashita — さよなら夏の日
yoyaku.text:
Summer doesn’t disappear all at once.

Tatsuro Yamashita — さよなら夏の日
(Sayonara Natsu no Hi)

A Japanese classic for that brief moment when summer starts turning into memory.

#TatsuroYamashita #山下達郎
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=tatsuro&song=sayonara-natsu-no-hi

machi.text:
Over a decade old, and somehow bigger every autumn.

The Neighbourhood — “Sweater Weather”

Cold air, a borrowed sweater, and a bassline that keeps its hands in its pockets.

#TheNeighbourhood
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=the-neighbourhood&song=sweater-weather

machi.midashi: Off Course — 秋の気配 (A Hint of Autumn)
machi.text:
In Japan, autumn is something you notice before you can see it.

Off Course — 秋の気配 (A Hint of Autumn)

A harbour town, a cooling afternoon, and something already over before anyone says it out loud.

#OffCourse
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=off-course&song=akifuchi

The song that turned a pop star into a folk singer.

Taylor Swift — “cardigan”

The first single from folklore. Piano, an old love story told from the middle of it, and the feeling of being someone’s favourite worn-out thing.

#TaylorSwift
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=taylor&song=cardigan

machi.midashi: Masayoshi Yamazaki — “One more time, One more chance”
machi.text:
In Japan this one comes with a warning: don’t play it unless you’re ready.

Masayoshi Yamazaki — “One more time, One more chance”

A man listing every place he still looks for someone who isn’t there.

#MasayoshiYamazaki
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=yamazaki-masayoshi&song=one-more-time-one-more-chance-1998-01-09

Summer ends. The song about it doesn’t.

Don Henley — “The Boys of Summer”

An empty beach in October, and a man who cannot stop looking backward. One of the great goodbyes to a season.

#DonHenley
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=don-henley&song=the-boys-of-summer

machi.midashi: Elephant Kashimashi — 今宵の月のように (Like Tonight’s Moon)
machi.text:
A song most of Japan knows, by a band most of the world has never heard.

Elephant Kashimashi — 今宵の月のように (Like Tonight’s Moon)

From 1997. An ordinary street, a bad day, and a voice that shouts hope.

#ElephantKashimashi
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=elephant-kashimashi&song=kon-ya-no-tsuki-no-yo-ni

machi.midashi: Yuuri — ドライフラワー (Dry Flower)
machi.text:
Dried flowers are the ones you keep long after they died.

Yuuri — ドライフラワー (Dry Flower)

A breakup song from Japan that admits the hardest part: you still think they were kind to you.

#Yuuri #優里
https://joy-relief-station.lovable.app/cover-guide?artist=yuuri&song=dry-flower
